stories.summary: Automotive designers are reintroducing mechanical controls after years of prioritizing touchscreens. Audi is among those shifting back, citing a need for usability and intuitive interactions. The industry is finding that advanced technology does not always deliver better results. Sometimes a button is just a button.

stories.title: The limits of AI in product design
stories.summary: Tech companies are increasingly embedding AI into physical products, from toothbrushes to household robots. Designers at Ideo are now questioning the necessity of this trend. While the industry assumes that adding AI is always an improvement, some products remain solutions in search of a problem.

stories.title: Retailers look to automate digital workflows
stories.summary: Live Story has launched a tool to integrate design systems, AI, and publishing for retail teams. The company claims this allows business units to manage digital experiences without relying on developers. Retailers are currently struggling with fragmented processes that slow down campaign launches and product page updates.

stories.summary: Tubik studio designed an editorial companion for HBO’s documentary The Alabama Solution, featuring an archive of over 1,300 death records. The team aimed to present multi-layered findings without relying on sensationalism. The design uses a neutral stone-colored bar to maintain readability across the site.

stories.title: Adobe previews Project Link Up for vector design
stories.summary: Adobe showcased Project Link Up at its MAX 2026 conference, a tool designed to turn standard dragging functions into context-aware fusion. The company claims the project will revolutionise vector design by automatically matching a scene's perspective. The feature remains a sneak peek for future software updates.

stories.title: AI video generator pricing remains varied
stories.summary: AI video generation has moved from early, flawed attempts to tools capable of producing photorealistic commercials and short films. Choosing a generator now requires balancing visual quality against diverse subscription models and platform limitations. The market has matured, but the cost of entry remains inconsistent across different providers.

stories.title: Adobe positions Firefly as an AI creative studio
stories.summary: Adobe is marketing the latest version of Firefly as an AI creative studio for any creator. The update includes an expanded AI agent, additional video tools, and a new design workspace. The company aims to keep users within the app for every stage of the creative process.

stories.title: Adobe demonstrates AI video editing tools
stories.summary: Adobe showcased ten experimental innovations at its annual MAX event, focusing on AI-driven workflows for film and design. Among the highlights was Project Scene Sweep, which aims to transform how creators edit video environments. These tools are currently in the prototype stage and may arrive in future updates.

stories.title: Adobe introduces Firefly Creative Agent
stories.summary: Adobe has updated Firefly to include a Creative Agent that manages multi-step tasks based on plain language instructions. Users can review the agent's plan and select specific AI models to execute the work. Adobe claims this workflow enables projects that were previously out of reach for its users.

stories.title: Disney expands Adobe AI partnership
stories.summary: Disney is expanding its existing partnership with Adobe to integrate AI tools across its theme parks, film production, and ESPN broadcasting divisions. The collaboration aims to leverage Adobe's creative software suite to support Disney's diverse media and entertainment operations. Further details were not provided in the announcement.

stories.title: Adobe previews real-time generative AI video editing
stories.summary: Adobe is showing off Project Live Set, a feature that allows editors to modify video effects while the footage plays. The tool is designed to provide an immediate feedback loop for changing subjects or environments. Adobe claims this is faster than standard generative models that require processing time.

stories.title: Adobe showcases experimental AI tools
stories.summary: Adobe revealed several experimental features at its MAX conference, including tools to turn 2D photos into 3D scenes and platforms for interviewing AI-generated characters. Project Screen Test aims to simplify the development of AI characters for video content. These tools are currently in the testing phase.

stories.title: Ludo platform targets AI game design
stories.summary: Ludo is a browser-based platform from Jet Play that uses AI to assist with game ideation and asset generation. It offers tools for creating sprites, 3D models, and audio. Annual pricing ranges from $180 for Indie users to $3,600 for Studio teams, with custom options for enterprise clients.

stories.title: Adobe ships Photoshop updates with AI agent support coming later
stories.summary: Adobe has released new AI tools for Photoshop and Premiere, including Relight and Generative Restyle. While many features are available now, integration with third-party AI agents via the Model Context Protocol is not expected until early 2027. The company continues to label several of these new tools as beta.

stories.title: Ideogram 4.0 targets text and layout
stories.summary: Ideogram 4.0 is a 9.3-billion-parameter open-weight model designed for users who need images to include specific text and layouts. The model treats text, colors, and structure as separate elements. It is available on Hugging Face for those creating posters, logos, or social media graphics.

stories.title: Adobe integrates more tools into Firefly
stories.summary: Adobe is updating its Firefly environment to include features previously reserved for its flagship applications. The company is positioning the platform as a starting point for routine creative tasks, allowing users to prototype websites and edit assets without opening the full Creative Cloud suite of professional software.

stories.title: Adobe adds AI relighting to Photoshop
stories.summary: Adobe has introduced new AI-assisted editing features to Photoshop, including tools to reposition light sources and generate stylistic variations. These features are currently rolling out across the company's creative applications. Premiere also received updates to its editing and audio tools during the Adobe MAX event.

stories.title: Adobe MAX 2026 highlights
stories.summary: Adobe held its annual MAX event in Miami Beach, focusing on new generative AI features for Creative Cloud. The company showcased updates for video and photo editing, alongside new agentic workflows. The event serves as a preview for the tools Adobe intends to integrate into its software suite.

stories.title: Adobe shifts to agentic workflows
stories.summary: Adobe announced that its Creative Cloud tools are moving toward agentic workflows, allowing users to delegate multi-step tasks to AI. The company is also enabling local integrations so third-party agents can control its software. New features include Generative Restyle in Photoshop and updated color modes for video editors.

stories.title: Adobe expands Firefly with design and workflow tools
stories.summary: Adobe has announced new features for Firefly, including tools for combining assets, building production workflows, and prototyping websites from natural-language prompts. The company aims to manage the entire creative lifecycle, from initial generation to final review, within the Firefly environment. These features were unveiled at Adobe MAX.

stories.title: Adobe to support external AI agents in Photoshop
stories.summary: Adobe announced it will integrate AI agents across its flagship products, allowing users to control editing tools through natural language. The company will also support the Model Context Protocol, enabling external agents like ChatGPT to interact with Adobe software. The features were unveiled at the Adobe MAX conference.

stories.title: AD Design Show returns to Mumbai
stories.summary: The 2026 edition of the AD Design Show will take place in Mumbai from November 13 to 15 at the Jio World Convention Centre. The event features curated collections from brands in the furniture, lighting, and decor sectors. Exhibitors include +NINE ONE, which focuses on functional decor pieces.

stories.summary: Three Mumbai-based creative professionals have been named finalists in the ADC Young Guns 24 competition. The contest celebrates emerging talent across creative industries, with the Indian finalists joining 94 individuals from 20 countries. The group includes Boomranng Studio, Chandni Poddar and Dhrutika Khimani.

stories.summary: Anthropic now allows users to open Adobe, Canva and Figma applications directly within Claude conversations. The update aims to let users edit photos, PDFs and designs without switching apps. Users can review edits as they happen, provided they stay within the Claude interface.

stories.summary: Plurai has raised $13 million in seed funding to build a platform that identifies failures in autonomous AI agents. The company claims it can catch issues before they reach customers. The platform is now generally available to developers with a free tier.

stories.summary: UK startup Fractile has raised $720 million in a Series C round, reaching a $7 billion valuation. The company is developing chips designed to run AI models but has not yet shipped a production product. Investors are betting on the future of purpose-built AI hardware.

stories.title: Canva announces job cuts while maintaining AI stance
stories.summary: Canva will cut or relocate up to 1200 workers, affecting one-fifth of its staff. CEO Melanie Perkins stated the firm needed to be refound following slowed growth. Despite the restructure, the company insists human tasks will not be replaced by artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Canva restructures with six months of pay for departing staff
stories.summary: Canva is cutting 1,271 roles, or 22 percent of its workforce, following a decade of growth. Departing staff receive six months of pay, a year of healthcare, and a 10,000 dollar grant for new ventures. The company describes the package as a benchmark for empathetic restructuring.

stories.title: Canva layoff memo draws praise and criticism
stories.summary: Canva announced a 22 percent workforce reduction on November 3. CEO Melanie Perkins called the move the hardest moment in the company history. While some observers labeled the communication a masterclass, others questioned the trend of celebrating corporate layoffs. The restructuring affects 1,271 employees.

stories.title: D&AD awards briefs encourage human creativity over AI
stories.summary: The D&AD New Blood Awards have launched briefs that ask students to prioritise human thinking over artificial intelligence. Brands including HSBC and JBL have explicitly restricted AI use in entries. The creative sector is currently adapting to rapid changes in technology and audience behaviour.

stories.title: Expertise may outweigh follower counts for creators
stories.summary: Recent podcast data suggests that expert guests often outperform those with large social media followings. Clips featuring authors and investigative journalists discussing complex topics have reached millions of views. The findings challenge the long-held assumption that audience size is the primary driver of content reach.

stories.title: Canva founders address leadership questions after job cuts
stories.summary: Canva founders Melanie Perkins and Cliff Obrecht addressed staff following the removal of nearly 1,300 roles. Obrecht stated the founders would step back if they were no longer fit to lead. Board members Bob Iger and Robyn Denholm attended the meeting to support the restructuring.

stories.title: Product manager roles rise as software hiring shifts
stories.summary: Data from TrueUp and Live Data Technologies indicates that open product manager roles are increasing while engineering demand stalls. Design postings have reached new lows as AI skills become more common in job descriptions. Tech hiring is increasingly concentrating within the Bay Area.

stories.title: Canva layoffs tested against company values
stories.summary: Canva is receiving attention for its approach to restructuring 22 percent of its workforce. Analysts suggest the process serves as a test of whether a company treatment of people aligns with its stated values. The firm combined internal communication with a financial support package for departing staff.

stories.title: Canva redundancy package receives mixed public reaction
stories.summary: Canva has been praised for an unusually generous redundancy package following plans to cut or relocate 22 percent of its staff. While some social media users called the response a masterclass in handling layoffs, others remain unconvinced by the praise. The package includes at least six months of pay.

research.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: BODYinTRANSIT-Lab: A Multimodal Dataset for Investigating Sensory-Driven Transformations in Body Perception and Affective Experiences
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal datasets that combine synchronised behavioural and physiological signals with subjective affective and body perception measures are still rare. This limits both the understanding of embodied experience and the development of computational models that infer subjective. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CUVE: Making Supervised Classification more Accessible through Visualization
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We present CUVE, an interface that enables people to build classifiers by generating visualizations that are interpretable by both humans and learning algorithms (the Visualization as Intermediate Representation approach). This UI enables users to create supervised. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools surface vulnerabilities early and their verdicts are rule-based and auditable. Yet developers routinely dismiss findings they cannot interpret. Large language models can supply the missing explanation, but designs that also. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Demonstration of MANA: Multi-perspective Alignment of NPC Agents
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We present MANA (Multi-perspective Alignment of NPC Agents), an interactive approach for authoring NPC behavior through embodied demonstration. We show MANA in the context of Minecraft, where a developer aligns NPCs while playing the game itself. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Designing Accessible and Rigorous ML Experiments: No-Code Visual Workflows and Structured Guidance for Beginners
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing machine learning (ML) experiments requires beginners to plan a methodologically sound workflow and implement it in a concrete environment. We evaluated two forms of support in two within-participant studies with 18 predominantly technically trained participants. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Designing UIs with GenAI: Understanding the Use, Benefits, and Limitations of Prompt-to-Design Generators
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of generative AI (GenAI) into user interface (UI) design has led to prompt-to-design generators (P2dGens), tools that enable designers to create UI prototypes from textual prompts efficiently. Despite their growing adoption, little is known. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Does Haptic Connection to a Healthy Partner Improve Motor Learning in Chronic Stroke? A Pilot Study of Robot-Based Dyadic Training
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Purpose: Robot-based haptic dyads, where two users exchange forces through robots, have been proposed for robot-assisted neurorehabilitation. This intervention could increase motor learning by promoting motor variability, providing an implicit communication channel, and facilitating social interaction. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
